subject: Business
title: Moats: What Protects a Business
description: A short lesson to help you apply Moats: What Protects a Business.

hook.text: Warren Buffett only invests in companies with moats — advantages competitors can't easily copy.

buildup.text: A moat can be a brand (Coca-Cola), network effects (Facebook), switching costs (Salesforce), or cost advantage.

discovery.text: Without a moat, any success attracts copycats. Profits get competed away within years.

twist.text: Moats erode over time. Kodak's moat was film expertise — which became worthless when digital arrived.

climax.text: The best companies don't just have moats. They actively widen them with every strategic decision.

punchline.text: Build something competitors can't copy, buy, or outspend.

quiz.question: What is a business moat?
options: A sustainable competitive advantage that protects profits
A legal patent on a product
A marketing campaign that goes viral

details.summary: A business moat is a sustainable competitive advantage that protects profits from competitors, analogous to a castle's moat. Warren Buffett identified moats including network effects, switching costs, cost advantages, intangible assets, and efficient scale as durable profit protectors.
details.whyItMatters: Companies without moats see profits competed away over time. Identifying and strengthening moats is essential for long-term value creation.
takeaways: Moats protect profits from competitive erosion over the long term
Key moat types include network effects, switching costs, and cost advantages
Buffett advises investing in companies with wide and durable moats

faq.question: What are the main types of business moats?
faq.answer: Network effects where more users increase value for all users. Switching costs that make changing expensive. Cost advantages from scale or unique resources. Intangible assets like brands, patents, and regulatory licenses. Efficient scale in markets that support only a few competitors.

faq.question: How can a company build a moat if it does not have one?
faq.answer: Build network effects by connecting users to each other. Create switching costs through data accumulation and integrations. Invest in brand building for premium pricing power. Pursue scale advantages through volume growth. Secure intellectual property through patents and proprietary processes.
